sense.text: America is in the Bible and is described in several ways, and this is one way to know that Babylon is America and the children of Israel are here. Revelation 18 continues from Revelation 17: “after these things” John sees the fall of the United States of America.

“Babylon the great is fallen, is fallen, and is become the habitation of devils”: lizards, alligators, unclean things like that. “The hold of every foul spirit”: foul spirits are caged here. “A cage of every unclean and hateful bird”: like owls and eagles.

“For all nations have drunk of the wine of the wrath of her fornication”: the wine of the wrath of her fornication is her political policies. Everybody obeys America. It ain’t talking about the Vatican; stop listening to these Christians. “And the kings of the earth have committed fornication with her, and the merchants of the earth are waxed rich”: that’s the proof. The merchants are their corporations, their companies, and nations only become rich “through the abundance of her delicacies”, dealing with the United States of America.

People like to bring up China. China was a third world country back in the 50s; how in the hell did they become a world superpower? America allowed them into the stock market, allowed them to buy, sell and trade with all nations, and now they are virtually number one in trade. People ask how come Africa, as large as the continent is, can’t compare to China. America does not allow Africa to do what they allow China to do. They don’t even allow Africa to manufacture their own weapons; that’s why there are no nuclear weapons in Africa. They got laws against that, but they don’t have that with China.

“Come out of her, my people”: so where are God’s people? In Babylon. “That ye be not partakers of her sins, and that ye receive not of her plagues.” And which tribe is it talking about? Zechariah 2 makes it more specific, tribe-wise.

precepts.why:
Revelation 18 continues from Revelation 17, so start there to know who is fallen. “The ten horns which thou sawest upon the beast” are the EU, the European common market: Belgium, Luxembourg, the Netherlands, Germany, the UK, Italy, Greece, France, Denmark, Ireland. The seven heads are Greece, Rome, Spain, France, Germany, Russia and Great Britain, and the eighth head is America. The great whore that sitteth upon many waters is America.

“These shall hate the whore, and shall make her desolate and naked, and shall eat her flesh, and burn her with fire.” The European Union will eventually turn on the United States of America. The disrespect President Trump showed toward them with the raising of tariffs, all that is good stuff. You might ask why he is doing that: God is creating his scenario for them to have hatred for America.

“For God hath put in their hearts to fulfil his will, and to agree, and give their kingdom unto the beast”: to support America, “until the words of God shall be fulfilled”, until prophecy is fulfilled.

“And the woman which thou sawest is that great city, which reigneth over the kings of the earth.” In case you didn’t know that was America, what other kingdom is reigning over all the kings of the earth? It’s the United States of America; verse 18 lets you know crystal clear. Some say it is the Vatican. No: the Arabs don’t respect the Vatican, Islam doesn’t respect the Vatican; they might wave their hand, and that’s about it. But everybody respects the United States of America whether they want to or not. So the Babylon that falls in Revelation 18 is America.

sense.text: “Come forth, and flee from the land of the north”: the land of the north is North America. That’s Babylon. “For I have spread you abroad as the four winds of the heaven, saith the Lord.”

“Deliver thyself, O Zion”. Zion is sometimes made reference to Jerusalem as a city, and sometimes to the twelve tribes, but Zion here is Judah. “That dwellest with the daughter of Babylon”: the daughter of Babylon is the children of Edom, the so-called white folks. So it is Judah dwelling with Edom.
“For he that toucheth you toucheth the apple of his eye”: he that toucheth Israel toucheth the apple of God’s eye. He was sent “unto the nations which spoiled you.”

“For, behold, I will shake mine hand upon them, and they shall be a spoil to their servants”: write this down, the servants there is us. God will shake his hand upon the nations, and the nations shall be a spoil to their servants. Right now we are their servants. “And ye shall know that the Lord of hosts hath sent me.”

So America is described as Babylon, the land of the north, and Judah is living here in the land of the north. Benjamin can go back to the Caribbean islands, Ephraim can go back to the Caribbean islands, Levi can go back to the Caribbean islands. It’s Judah that’s always here.

precepts.why: Zion is also used of one tribe: “But chose the tribe of Judah, the mount Zion which he loved.” That is what Zechariah 2:7 is talking about. “Deliver thyself, O Zion” is Judah.

Who is the daughter of Babylon that Judah dwells with? “Remember, O Lord, the children of Edom”: E-D-O-M, that’s the red people, what y’all call so-called white folks. “In the day of Jerusalem; who said, Rase it, rase it”: rase means destroy. Destroy it, destroy it, “even to the foundation thereof.”

Then see what it calls Edom: “O daughter of Babylon, who art to be destroyed”, destined to be destroyed. “Happy shall he be, that rewardeth thee as thou hast served us.” So Zion, Judah, is dwelling with Edom, the daughter of Babylon.

“And this is the blessing of Judah: and he said, Hear, Lord, the voice of Judah”: Judah is going to be the teachers. “And bring him unto his people”: Judah would be the one the spirit comes on first, to go and gather the tribes. “Let his hands be sufficient for him; and be thou an help to him from his enemies.”

With that read, go back to Zechariah 2:7: “Deliver thyself, O Zion, that dwellest with the daughter of Babylon.” It is Judah, in Babylon, that God delivers from his enemies to gather his people.

A precept to explain it further, because the wording of Zechariah might be somewhat difficult: “Surely Moab shall be as Sodom, and the children of Ammon as Gomorrah, even the breeding of nettles, and saltpits, and a perpetual desolation: the residue of my people shall spoil them”. See that? The residue of God’s people shall spoil them. “And the remnant of my people shall possess them”: possess, meaning own those nations.

So when Zechariah says “they shall be a spoil to their servants”, the servants are Israel. Today we are their servants; then the nations shall be a spoil to us.

sense.text: Here is another description of America in the Bible; you just have to know where to look. “Thus saith the Lord God concerning Edom”: remember what we read in Zechariah, that the daughter of Babylon is the children of Edom. “An ambassador is sent among the heathen”: among the nations somebody is going to rise up and say, “Arise ye, and let us rise up against her in battle.” Let’s go against America and her allies, against Israel.

“Behold, I have made thee small among the heathen: thou art greatly despised.” America is small, just like Israel is small. The dark nations of the earth are like three quarters of the earth; Esau is less than one quarter. Put up the map of the land of Israel: in the Arab world, that tiny speck is Israel, the fake Israelis, small among the heathen.

And they are greatly despised. All the evil that fake Israel is leading America to do has all nations pissed off; people are asking why America is obeying Israel, destroying countries. They have to do it, so that their prophecy can be fulfilled. All nations are turning against America and against the Israelis, because it’s Bible prophecy.

“The pride of thine heart hath deceived thee”: Make America Great Again. They said all nations have got to pay their wages when it comes to America. Trump is pushing people out of the way, nations’ delegates out of the way, to get his seat.

“Thou that dwellest in the clefts of the rock” goes back into history. In the time of Genesis 36 they dwelt at Mount Seir, but it is not referring to that solely. In the Middle Ages they lived in the Caucasus mountains of Georgia, Russia. That is why they call themselves Caucasian: Jewish Caucasian, Russian Caucasian, English Caucasian, American Caucasian, Australian Caucasian, South African Caucasian, Dutch Caucasian. With that word they are telling you they come from the Caucasus mountains.

“Whose habitation is high”: they like skyscrapers. “That saith in his heart, Who shall bring me down to the ground?” In other words, who can conquer me, who can whip my behind? To make a statement like that you have to have something to back it up, and America has the arsenal, the weaponry, to say nobody can conquer us.

“Though thou exalt thyself as the eagle”: not only would Edom be prideful and have power, their symbol would be the eagle. It ain’t the Chinese; it’s the United States of America. The great seal of the United States is the eagle, with arrows in one claw representing war and the olive branch in the other for peace. They come to you with peace, but war is in their heart.

“And though thou set thy nest among the stars”: that is space travel. That ain’t China, that ain’t Africa, that ain’t the Arabs; that’s the United States of America. When they landed on the moon in ’69 they said, The eagle has landed. “Thence will I bring thee down, saith the Lord.” Since the 1960s the truth has been coming out like never before. Vietnam kicked them out of the country: America said we could blow them to hell and back, but then we’re going to lose the poppy seeds, so let’s just retreat.

“If thieves came to thee, if robbers by night”, “would they not have stolen till they had enough?” A regular thief steals till he has enough, but not this white man, not America in particular, and not even the fake Israelis, because it goes into both of them. They take more and more and more; there’s no satisfying them. “If the grapegatherers came to thee, would they not leave some grapes?” A grape gatherer leaves some grapes behind.

“How are the things of Esau searched out!” Esau doesn’t leave anything behind. He takes every grape, the stem, the root, the ground the grape was in; he takes everything.

“How are his hidden things sought up!” The evils Esau has done are being sought out now. A lot of the evil America has done is surfacing: only recently it came out what they did at Lake Lanier in Georgia, drowning those towns, and at Seneca Village, where Central Park is, where they tore it up and murdered us out of there.

“All the men of thy confederacy have brought thee even to the border: the men that were at peace with thee have deceived thee”. This goes back to Revelation 17:16, read at the start: the men of thy confederacy are the European Union, the ten horns that shall hate the whore. Do you think the EU is going to let America get away with all those tariffs, all the disrespect America gives them? Don’t fool yourselves. “And prevailed against thee”: they are going to prevail against America.

“For as ye have drunk upon my holy mountain”: notice it goes from America to Israel, because America and these fake Israelis are working together. How did they drink upon the holy mountain? Murder, bloodshed. The white man ran us out of the land, out of the country, and when they came back in 1948 they brought murder and bloodshed to the Palestinians.

“So shall all the heathen drink continually, yea, they shall drink, and they shall swallow down, and they shall be as though they had not been.” These nations shall be as though they had not been. That is America in the Bible.

“The eagle, whom thou sawest come up from the sea, is the kingdom which was seen in the vision of thy brother Daniel.” Daniel 7 speaks of the fourth kingdom, more dreadful than all the kingdoms before it, but Daniel doesn’t give its animal symbol. Ezra gives it: the animal symbol is the eagle, and America is included in that kingdom near the end. So America is described there too.

America is celebrating its 250th anniversary, two and a half centuries since the Declaration of Independence in 1776, with a nationwide prayer vigil, just as Israel did: Israel started theirs the evening before for judgment, then the morning for mercy, then twelve noon to increase our faith. America is doing the same thing, praying to their demon god. They are praying to Satan. You thought we prayed to the same God? No.

“For my love they are my adversaries: but I give myself unto prayer.” Like David said, we have to give ourselves unto prayer.

“And they have rewarded me evil for good, and hatred for my love.” They have rewarded our people evil for good. They tell us pull yourself up by your bootstraps, get away from us, we don’t want you drinking our water, in our schools. So we got away: we set up Greenwood, we set up Rosewood, we set up Seneca Village. Then they said, they’re doing better than us; let’s bomb them, let’s drown them out, destroy their economy. And then: why don’t you pull yourself up by your bootstraps? Y’all don’t see the hypocrisy in that. As soon as they tell us to get away from them, we get away, we do our own thing and we survive, and then they say they’ve got to destroy us. And none of these great black intellects get on the news and bring that out.
“Set thou a wicked man over him: and let Satan stand at his right hand.” This goes back to Genesis 4:7: the wicked man is Satan, and Satan stands at his right hand.

“When he shall be judged, let him be condemned: and let his prayer become sin.” Prayer has become sin for them. All their prayers are sin; God ain’t accepting their prayers, according to the Holy Bible.

For America’s 250th, white nationalists marched on the nation’s capital, masked, carrying Confederate flags. Black Christians think white Christians and them are together. No. These white nationalist Christians told Myron straight out: when we get rid of all these immigrants and these blacks, you’ve got to go too. That’s how they all do. There are the suckers they use to push their agenda, who don’t know they are suckers, and there are the ones they openly tell, we hate y’all. Even in the Israelite community some keep saying there are good ones and we have to save some of them; they’re going to get a rude awakening. All through the scriptures God is saying he is going to exalt the nation of Israel to make them his chosen people. If you say, no, we don’t care what they did to us, there are some good ones and you need to save them, you hate God.

This verse is about the Berlin Conference. A Christian will try to hem you up, so understand: it started with the Greeks when they began dividing up the lands. The four generals of Alexander, Ptolemy, Lysimachus, Cassander and Seleucus, divided up the lands, and white folks continued that same thing.

“Thus shall he do in the most strong holds with a strange god.” Many of you think the white man serves the same God we read about. No. The Bible says they serve a strange god: Cesare Borgia. Back then it was Zeus or whatever; today it is this one. A strange god, a god that looks like them, that doesn’t mind genocide, doesn’t mind mass murder, doesn’t mind GMOs in the food murdering the people, doesn’t mind redlining, doesn’t mind the school to prison pipeline. That’s that religion. The strange god is their white god.

“Whom he shall acknowledge and increase with glory: and he shall cause them to rule over many”: the nations, especially Africa. “And shall divide the land for gain”: they divided Africa for gain, financial gain. That’s the Berlin Conference.

On their 250th the heat waves came: millions under heat alerts, celebrations cancelled or delayed, and in France and across Europe a record number dying from the heat, fighting over air conditioners. Who controls the sun? God. Keep praying, keep fasting.

Never forget that we were slaves on July 4th, 1776. You might think the country has changed.

“And they shall scoff at the kings”: when the white man came throughout the Americas, they scoffed at the kings that were already set up here. “And the princes shall be a scorn unto them”: they scorned the princes set up here. “They shall deride every strong hold”: every stronghold they found, they took it down. “For they shall heap dust”: confusion; they heaped religious confusion. “And take it”: they took the land by violence.

“Then shall his mind change.” His mind changed around the 60s, when we got the civil rights. Remember the signs: no dogs, negroes or Mexicans. After the civil rights they said, let’s appear to be gentler, kinder, more Christian; we’ll let you in our schools, you can sit on the same toilet with me, you can sit next to me in a restaurant, for the time being. Under Obama and then Biden they got religion out of the schools; you couldn’t say God bless you, you had to say happy holidays. Then Trump came: they had sixty-something years, and he is sick of us, and of the Spanish people too, putting them out of the country, even sending a lady from Venezuela to Sudan. So things are changing now.

“And he shall pass over, and offend, imputing this his power unto his god.” His god is the strange god we just read about in Daniel 11:39. It is not the same God we read about in the Bible. Although they say it is, it is not.

And y’all be thinking things have changed. Police officers in Montreal were investigated for targeting black and Arab people, and for cutting off black people’s locks and keeping them as trophies. Things haven’t changed; they’ve been keeping it secret, and now it’s coming out.

Job sees America’s 250th anniversary. The prophet Job is a true man, but he is also a metaphorical representation of the fall of the twelve tribes of Israel. “There was a man in the land of Uz, whose name was Job; and that man was perfect and upright, and one that feared God, and eschewed evil.”
“And his sons went and feasted in their houses, every one his day”: every one his day means their birthday.
“For Job said, It may be that my sons have sinned, and cursed God in their hearts”: Job knew what his sons were doing. “Thus did Job continually.”

“Now there was a day when the sons of God came to present themselves before the Lord”: these sons of God are the angels. They are not the same sons of God as in Genesis 6. In Genesis 6 those sons of God are our people, before we were called Israelites; we were called sons of God. For some reason that blows a Christian’s mind.

“Hast not thou made an hedge about him, and about his house, and about all that he hath on every side? thou hast blessed the work of his hands, and his substance is increased in the land.” Job’s life was blessed; Satan is bringing all the truth out to the Lord.
“Behold, all that he hath is in thy power; only upon himself put not forth thine hand.” The Lord lets Satan try him, but Satan may not touch him himself.

Here is the first trial, dealing with his businesses and finances: “The oxen were plowing, and the asses feeding beside them: And the Sabeans fell upon them, and took them away”, and slew the servants.
The second trial, where Satan again hits his business and his finances: “The fire of God is fallen from heaven, and hath burned up the sheep, and the servants, and consumed them”.
The third trial: “The Chaldeans made out three bands, and fell upon the camels, and have carried them away”.

The fourth trial deals with Job’s family: “Thy sons and thy daughters were eating and drinking wine in their eldest brother’s house: And, behold, there came a great wind from the wilderness, and smote the four corners of the house, and it fell upon the young men, and they are dead”. Now Job’s kids are dead.

precepts.why:
“But put forth thine hand now, and touch all that he hath, and he will curse thee to thy face” goes with this: “My son, if thou come to serve the Lord, prepare thy soul for temptation.”

As soon as we give our life to the Lord, the Lord forgives us of our sins; we repent, and now we start to do the work. We get involved, we study, we clean our lives up according to the commandments. And the Lord is sitting on the throne, and Satan comes up and says, Have you considered my servant such and such, or sister such and such? They’re doing real well right now, but I guarantee you, if you let me do A, B or C to them, they’re going to curse you. They’re going to leave the truth, blaspheme your name, and go right back to me and white Jesus. And the Lord says, All right, go ahead, you can try. Don’t kill them; don’t take their life. That is Job, and that is us.

sense.text: “Behold, he is in thine hand; but save his life”: don’t take his life.
“So went Satan forth from the presence of the Lord, and smote Job with sore boils from the sole of his foot unto his crown.” That was the fifth trial: his health. Job’s health was in decline.

precepts.why:
Job’s life represents the twelve tribes of Israel. “The ox knoweth his owner, and the ass his master’s crib: but Israel doth not know, my people doth not consider”: we don’t consider our God, who our God is, or our habitation.

“Ah sinful nation”: he calls us a sinful nation, “a people laden with iniquity, a seed of evildoers, children that are corrupters: they have forsaken the Lord, they have provoked the Holy One of Israel unto anger, they are gone away backward.” We went backward, backsliding.

“The whole head is sick, and the whole heart faint. From the sole of the foot even unto the head there is no soundness in it”: no soundness from the top of our head to the bottom of our feet, “but wounds, and bruises, and putrifying sores”, like Job had.

So what Job went through, we go through as a nation of people. Why? Because we were the servants of God, and when the trials came, we lost. We gave up. We gave into sin. We turned our back on the Lord.

sense.text: “Then Eliphaz the Temanite answered and said”: these are Job’s friends. “But who can withhold himself from speaking?”
“Behold, thou hast instructed many”: Eliphaz says to Job, you have instructed many. “And thou hast strengthened the weak hands”: you were the one who strengthened men and women when they were weak.

“Thy words have upholden him that was falling”: your words upheld those who fell down in grief, and in sin. “And thou hast strengthened the feeble knees”: you were the one, Job, who strengthened the feeble knees.

“But now it is come upon thee, and thou faintest”: now judgment has come upon you, Job, and now you’ve given up, you’ve lost the spirit. Where’s that mighty man who helped all the people? Now you’re upset, your lips stuck out, you’ve got an attitude. “It toucheth thee, and thou art troubled.”

precepts.why: Something we should all be mindful of: “There is one that is wise and teacheth many, and yet is unprofitable to himself.” That is what Eliphaz was telling Job: you were the one who comforted everybody, but now that your turn has come, now that judgment has come upon you, you’re fainting, you want to give up.

sense.text: Who exactly was Job? In the 29th chapter Job is speaking about his own life. “Oh that I were as in months past, as in the days when God preserved me”: when my life was good, my kids were with me, my businesses were flourishing. Why can’t it be like in the days past?
“When his candle shined upon my head”: the Holy Spirit was on him. “And when by his light I walked through darkness”: like Job, we can only walk through darkness with God’s commandments.
“As I was in the days of my youth, when the secret of God was upon my tabernacle”: God reveals his secrets to the Israelites. It shows the relationship between Job and us.
“When the Almighty was yet with me, when my children were about me”: he’s recollecting.
“When I washed my steps with butter”: a smooth life; his life was good. “And the rock poured me out rivers of oil.”
“When I went out to the gate through the city, when I prepared my seat in the street”: Job was a judge.
“The young men saw me, and hid themselves: and the aged arose, and stood up.” Remember, he is speaking of times past.

“The princes refrained talking, and laid their hand on their mouth.” When Job rolled on the scene, everybody shut the hell up. Princes covered their mouths, young men moved the hell out of the way, and the old men stood up and saluted Job. This is some powerful stuff. “The nobles held their peace, and their tongue cleaved to the roof of their mouth”: they had nothing to say either.
“When the ear heard me, then it blessed me; and when the eye saw me, it gave witness to me”: that’s total respect and honor.

Now Job tells you what he used to do: “Because I delivered the poor that cried, and the fatherless, and him that had none to help him.” The fatherless are the orphans. This is what Eliphaz was making reference to: you helped all these people when they were down and out, but now it’s come on you. In chapter 29 Job is reflecting on his life.

“The blessing of him that was ready to perish came upon me”: when somebody is about to die and wants to speak to you, sometimes you’re at a loss for words; you don’t know what to say to bring them comfort so they can transition. Job was that type of man; he knew exactly what to say. “And I caused the widow’s heart to sing for joy”: then you have to comfort the widow. She’s mourning, she’s crying, her husband just died, and Job knew just what to say.

That is another level, where you have to go to the Lord: give me the words. People call, they are crying on the other end, and you have to give comforting words. You might think it’s easy; it ain’t easy. How do you let someone who is about to die know it’s going to be okay, that even if you leave this world you’re going to be all right? You have to train yourself to do it. We all have to believe that when we die, that’s not the end of it for us, and that is going to comfort us.
“I put on righteousness, and it clothed me: my judgment was as a robe and a diadem”: that shows how Job used to dress. The way he dressed reflected his righteousness.

“I was eyes to the blind, and feet was I to the lame. I was a father to the poor: and the cause which I knew not I searched out.” Whatever Job didn’t know, he searched it out. Sometimes brothers try to fake stuff; don’t fake it. That was Job’s attribute, and we have to be the same way. Get the Who’s Who with the Apocrypha, the Zondervan Bible dictionary, the Complete Works of Josephus, a concordance. Before you ask us a question, search it out, then ask your question after you’ve done your research.

“And I brake the jaws of the wicked, and plucked the spoil out of his teeth”: whatever the wicked took, Job took it back from him. You stole something, I’m taking it back from you. I bet you didn’t know that about Job. That’s forefather Job right there.
“My root was spread out by the waters, and the dew lay all night upon my branch”: his family was large.
“Unto me men gave ear, and waited, and kept silence at my counsel.” Job was up there. He wasn’t no pushover, he wasn’t no punk.

“After my words they spake not again”: after Job spoke, you had nothing to say. “And they waited for me as for the rain; and they opened their mouth wide as for the latter rain”: they waited for his words with their mouths open when he was teaching and giving counsel. He was dropping blessings on them, understanding.
“If I laughed on them, they believed it not”: that shows you he had an austere spirit.

“I chose out their way”: he counseled them, he directed them. “And sat chief, and dwelt as a king in the army, as one that comforteth the mourners.” Job sat like a king in the army. I bet we didn’t know that about Job.

precepts.why: “By his light I walked through darkness”: what does that mean? “For the commandment is a lamp; and the law is light; and reproofs of instruction are the way of life”. Now we understand what Job is talking about: the light he walked by is God’s commandments and law. Like Job, we can only walk through darkness with God’s commandments.

“When the secret of God was upon my tabernacle”: “The secret things belong unto the Lord our God: but those things which are revealed belong unto us and to our children for ever, that we may do all the words of this law.” God reveals his secrets to the Israelites. The secret of God was upon Job’s tabernacle, and that shows the relationship between Job and us.

“When I prepared my seat in the street”: what does that mean? “Judges and officers shalt thou make thee in all thy gates”, “and they shall judge the people with just judgment.” Job went out to the gate and prepared his seat: Job was a judge.

Delivering the fatherless goes into God’s law: “He doth execute the judgment of the fatherless and widow, and loveth the stranger, in giving him food and raiment.” Job did what God’s law says God does: he delivered the poor that cried, the fatherless, him that had none to help him, and he caused the widow’s heart to sing for joy.

“I put on righteousness, and it clothed me”: “Let thy priests be clothed with righteousness; and let thy saints shout for joy.” That’s why it was written down: Job was clothed with righteousness, as God’s priests are to be.

“The cause which I knew not I searched out”: “Search the scriptures; for in them ye think ye have eternal life: and they are they which testify of me.” Whatever you don’t know, search it out; don’t fake it.

“These were more noble than those in Thessalonica, in that they received the word with all readiness of mind, and searched the scriptures daily, whether those things were so.” That was the attribute Job had, and we have to be the same way. We have to get to that point: search it out, search, and ask your question after you’ve done your research.

“Unto me men gave ear, and waited, and kept silence at my counsel”: “Hearken now unto my voice, I will give thee counsel, and God shall be with thee: Be thou for the people to God-ward, that thou mayest bring the causes unto God”. That’s what Job was doing: giving counsel, and bringing the causes of the people unto God.

“They opened their mouth wide as for the latter rain” is saying the same thing as Moses: “My doctrine shall drop as the rain, my speech shall distil as the dew, as the small rain upon the tender herb, and as the showers upon the grass”. When Job spoke, it was like that. And that right there is prophetic; it is going to come in the future, near to come.

sense.text: “And I will turn my hand upon thee”: God will turn his hand upon the Israelites; the thee is us, you and me. “And purely purge away thy dross”: dross is waste, refuse, any worthless matter. All that is within us that is wasteful and useless: sins, adultery, lying, child molestation, masturbation, pornography, stealing, bestiality, anger, malice, all of that. “And take away all thy tin”: the tin goes with the dross; it is the waste that’s within us. That one verse speaks volumes. And for the dross to be purged away, we have to go through some stuff.

“And I will restore thy judges as at the first, and thy counsellors as at the beginning”: God is going to restore the judges of Israel as at the first: in the time of Moses, and before Moses, when we were little gods on the earth. “Afterward thou shalt be called, The city of righteousness, the faithful city.”
“Zion shall be redeemed with judgment, and her converts with righteousness.”
“And the destruction of the transgressors and of the sinners shall be together”: wicked Israel is going to get the same judgment as Esau. “And they that forsake the Lord shall be consumed.”
“For they shall be ashamed of the oaks which ye have desired”: the oaks are the idols. “And ye shall be confounded for the gardens that ye have chosen”: the gardens are the churches.
“For ye shall be as an oak whose leaf fadeth”: your understanding is gone. “And as a garden that hath no water”: no water of understanding for you.

“And the strong shall be as tow”: useless. “And the maker of it as a spark”: like firewood. “And they shall both burn together, and none shall quench them”: nobody is going to quench it. You’re going to be put to death; God is going to get rid of you, because he can’t use you.

precepts.why: Christ tells what dross and tin are. “For from within, out of the heart of men”, out of the mind of men, “proceed evil thoughts”: that’s dross and tin. Adulteries, fornications, murders, thefts, covetousness, wickedness, deceit, lasciviousness, an evil eye, blasphemy, pride, foolishness: dross and tin, every one of them. “All these evil things come from within, and defile the man.” That is what God turns his hand upon us to purge away.

For the dross to be purged away we have to go through some stuff. “We glory in tribulations also”: when you read Paul in Hebrews 12, Paul tells you nobody rejoices in tribulation, but here he is giving you the after effect. “Knowing that tribulation worketh patience”: that tribulation goes back to Ecclesiasticus 2:1, when you come to serve the Lord, prepare thy soul for temptation. That’s hard times. When you go through hell, you learn patience.

“And patience, experience”: a lot of us come into this truth with no experience. Some of you are 50, 40, 30, and you have experiences in the world, but in the truth of God you have no experience. That’s the experience you need. “And experience, hope: And hope maketh not ashamed”: hope makes us not ashamed, because we endure to the end, “because the love of God is shed abroad in our hearts by the Holy Ghost which is given unto us.”

Purging has another precept, a heavy one. “But in a great house”: the great house is Israel, the nation of Israel, the twelve tribes. “There are not only vessels of gold and of silver”: in every IUIC school, Philly, DC, Virginia, New York, Atlanta, Connecticut, OKC, there are men and women who are gold and silver, and it is up to you to discern and identify who they are. “But also of wood and of earth”: in every school there are brothers and sisters who ain’t right. “And some to honour”, the gold and the silver, “and some to dishonour”: those are the ones that are not right.

That is not the new brothers and new sisters who just walked through the door; we know we’re not right when we walk in. It is the men and women who have been in this truth for years and have not changed: still murmurers, gossipers, putting forth no work, no effort to study and learn and improve their own lives. To them it’s a social club: come hang out with the homeboys, drink a little wine, go home and play dominoes.

“If a man therefore purge himself from these”: see the word purge. You have to know your circle. When Bishop Nathanyel came into the truth he had a circle of five or six brothers and was always getting in trouble around them: one went to pull his so-called wife out of a lesbian club and nearly got into a fist fight with a group of lesbians; they jumped the turnstile, and the police grabbed him, found his Bible and told him to try reading Romans 13 and obey the power. He had to change his circle of brothers and be around leadership, around the elders, so he could learn and get his mind right.

“He shall be a vessel unto honour, sanctified, and meet for the master’s use”: then God can use you. You want to get to the point where we can say, send that brother to this city or that state and he can turn it up; like Isaiah said to the Lord, send me. Don’t worry about hurting people’s feelings: if you know they ain’t right, separate from them. They’re always murmuring, gossiping, with some plan to mess everything up. You have to be spiritually inclined enough to understand that the vessels of dishonor are here to try you. Every bird cleaves to its like; see who groups together. Separate yourself from the brothers and sisters who are murmuring and not taking the truth seriously, and let the Lord do his thing.

That also explains why we cannot join with the other camps: cookouts on the Sabbath, saying it’s okay to rape girls, stealing money from the school to buy their wives Maseratis and Mercedes, beating up the baby mamas. Based on what we just read, it’s impossible. Only a fool would do that.

sense.text: “By reason of the multitude of oppressions they make the oppressed to cry: they cry out by reason of the arm of the mighty.” This is Elihu speaking to Job prophetically about the times to come. Are we not oppressed today? Yes.

precepts.why: Crushed and oppressed always: “And thou shalt grope at noonday, as the blind gropeth in darkness, and thou shalt not prosper in thy ways: and thou shalt be only oppressed and spoiled evermore”. This is what Elihu was talking about: the multitude of oppressions that make the oppressed cry is the curse Moses spoke upon us.

This is King Solomon speaking prophetically: “So I returned, and considered all the oppressions that are done under the sun: and behold the tears of such as were oppressed”. That’s what Moses talked about; Solomon is saying the same thing. “And they had no comforter”: looking for justice in all the wrong places. “And on the side of their oppressors there was power”: they have the guns, they have the nuclear weapons, they have the court system. They have it all; we have nothing. “But they had no comforter.”

“For he hath looked down from the height of his sanctuary; from heaven did the Lord behold the earth”. What does he see? “To hear the groaning of the prisoner”: we’re the prisoner. You know what it is like to be the son of God and be in prison: in a weak body, ruled and dominated by a wicked race of people, subject to their laws. “To loose those that are appointed to death”: God is going to loose those that are appointed to death.

“For we know that the whole creation groaneth and travaileth in pain together until now”: just as we groan, all creation groans. “And not only they, but ourselves also, which have the firstfruits of the Spirit”: the firstfruits of the Spirit is Christ. “Even we ourselves groan within ourselves, waiting for the adoption, to wit, the redemption of our body.” We want our godhood back. We want rulership back, we want dominion back. We want to reign on this planet like we once did. That’s what we want.

sense.text:
So what happened? Why is it hard for our people? Esau figured out the psychology that image is everything: if they can see it, they will believe it. When the Huxtables were on, and then A Different World, black college enrollment went up some thirty percent; when they took that off the air and put up Lil Wayne and the rappers, it declined. If these negroes can see themselves in greatness, they will become that. So they put the lowest of black society in the forefront, in all the media, globally, and they destroy or remake every black show that had a positive note for our people. That’s why the AI department, the art and the video team are so important: to put positive images out there. What you think is what white people programmed you to think.

“I was wroth with my people”: God was mad with us because we broke his laws, his commandments. “I have polluted mine inheritance, and given them into thine hand”: he scattered us among the nations. Who is the thine? Verse 1 tells you: “O virgin daughter of Babylon”. The daughter of Babylon is Edom, as we read in Psalms 137.

“Thou didst shew them no mercy”: the white man showed us no mercy here. “Upon the ancient hast thou very heavily laid thy yoke”: even upon the older men and women they laid a heavy yoke. That is how they polluted us: they gave us Christmas, they gave us all that filth and evil.

precepts.why:
“And the Lord shall scatter thee among all people”: all people means exactly what it says, even among Amalek. In the documentary Little White Lie, a girl raised white, who thought she was Jewish, light-skinned with wavy hair, thick lips and a wide nose, learned at the end that her father was a black man. She is Israel, our people. That’s why we have to be mindful what we say. Just teach, and let the spirit handle the rest.

“From the one end of the earth even unto the other; and there thou shalt serve other gods, which neither thou nor thy fathers have known, even wood and stone”: Christianity and Islam, the world’s two largest religions.

“And among these nations shalt thou find no ease”: don’t think we had it easy among the Arabs; the Arabs were castrating us. “Neither shall the sole of thy foot have rest”: we had no rest wherever we were; in China they got us drunk and were murdering us. “But the Lord shall give thee there a trembling heart, and failing of eyes, and sorrow of mind”.

“And thy life shall hang in doubt before thee”: we thought when we got emancipated we were free. Juneteenth. Then the white man cut two holes in a sheet and put on the white robe: the KKK, from the capirotes of Spain in the Inquisition. Spain was in this country, and what they took from over there they brought here; Google, run by Amalek, will say there is no resemblance, but don’t believe the hype. As soon as we thought we were free, they gave us hell.

“And thou shalt fear day and night, and shalt have none assurance of thy life”: imagine this. You build a town because white folks don’t want you drinking their water or going to their schools. You’ve got your own cab company, your own hospital, your own bank, black, black, black. Then a white girl says somebody raped her, and they drop dynamite on the city from planes and murder a lot of us. Watch the first episode of Watchmen with Regina King; it goes into the history of Tulsa. In that same film a projector plays a hidden message, kill, hate each other, and the people in the theater turn violent. That is real: they put it in the music and what we watch, and then ask why black people are so violent. Train your children not to look at that or listen to that.

“In the morning thou shalt say, Would God it were even! and at even thou shalt say, Would God it were morning!” In the morning we say, Lord, let this day go by quick; at night we wish it were morning, “for the fear of thine heart wherewith thou shalt fear, and for the sight of thine eyes which thou shalt see.” What did we see? Hangings, mutilation, lynchings, bombings. We saw it all.

“And the Lord shall bring thee into Egypt again with ships”: slave ships, “by the way whereof I spake unto thee”: the way Moses said it would happen is how it happened. “Thou shalt see it no more again”: we would not see ancient Egypt any more. “And there ye shall be sold unto your enemies for bondmen and bondwomen”: once we got off those ships we were sold unto our enemies, slave men and slave women. “And no man shall buy you”: no man shall save us, redeem us from the curses God put on us. There is only one redeemer, brothers and sisters, and that’s Christ.

“Thou didst shew them no mercy”: “And I am very sore displeased with the heathen that are at ease: for I was but a little displeased, and they helped forward the affliction.” God was a little displeased with us, and they afflicted us more and more and more. That’s what God is saying right there.

sense.text:
“Thy sons have fainted, they lie at the head of all the streets”: that’s why our young men hang on the corners. “As a wild bull in a net”: uncontrollable. Our young men are like wild bulls in a net; it’s a trap, this system is a trap. “They are full of the fury of the Lord, the rebuke of thy God”: the fury of the Lord is Deuteronomy 28:15-68, the curses God put upon us, and they are on our young men.

In Queens, across the street from a house the family looked at, was a playground with some twenty cute little kids running around. Time went by, those little kids grew up, and they were having shootouts, bullets flying through the house, the wife and the children thrown on the floor. That is what they turned into.

“Therefore hear now this, thou afflicted, and drunken, but not with wine”: we are an afflicted people. Look at the news: we are afflicted from sun up to sun down, over and over. You can turn a blind eye to it, but it’s there. And we are drunk, but not with wine. Drunk with what? Lies, religions, falsehood. Some of us believe in these false Christian religions, Islam, politics; we’re drunk on philosophy out here.

“Thus saith thy Lord the Lord, and thy God that pleadeth the cause of his people”: he alone pleads our cause. “Behold, I have taken out of thine hand the cup of trembling”: that’s Deuteronomy 28:68, and that’s why we’re waking up now. “Even the dregs of the cup of my fury”: the dregs are the bottom, the few drops left after you drink it all. “Thou shalt no more drink it again”: after this captivity, it is over.

“But I will put it into the hand of them that afflict thee”: that’s the nations, starting with Esau. “Which have said to thy soul, Bow down, that we may go over”: lower yourself, humiliate yourself; let us walk all over you, let us disrespect you. Even if it looks like slavery times, just do it, I’ll give you a quarter. In the old photos we were forced to carry Esau on our backs, and today some of our people in Africa carry white tourists on their backs for 25 cents. African dignity or tourism for dollars: why don’t they respect you? Because you’re carrying a white man around for a quarter.

“And thou hast laid thy body as the ground, and as the street, to them that went over.” Look at the black people, even churches praying and fasting, who cried for Charlie Kirk. They never met him; he never said anything nice for our people, never helped our people. That is a perfect example of Isaiah 51:23: our people will cry for white people, but won’t cry for each other.

precepts.why: The fury of the Lord on our sons: “The Lord shall smite thee with madness, and blindness, and astonishment of heart”. Some of our young men are mentally deranged. The ones doing that drill music are murderers, killers, and don’t care.

Wine represents falsehood: “If a man walking in the spirit and falsehood do lie, saying, I will prophesy unto thee of wine and of strong drink; he shall even be the prophet of this people.” Wine and strong drink symbolize lies. So when Isaiah says we are “drunken, but not with wine”, we are drunk with lies, with religion, with falsehood.

sense.text:
The whole world is anti-black. In Libya there is an open air slave market where Africans are kidnapped, pulled off the boats and sold, and our sisters are auctioned. Don’t let the Christians say Deuteronomy 28:68 ain’t still going on; we just saw it. Deuteronomy 28:64 and on still exists over there. We have to repent of our sins. The Lord is releasing us from those curses over here so we can get our minds right toward him and have the word spread from here to there.

“Thou hast given us like sheep appointed for meat; and hast scattered us among the heathen”: that is what we read in Deuteronomy 28:64, scattered among the heathen.

“Thou sellest thy people for nought”: God sold us for nothing. “And dost not increase thy wealth by their price”: God wasn’t looking for money when we were sold. He allowed us to be sold, but he was not looking for financial gain for himself.

“Thou makest us a reproach to our neighbours, a scorn and a derision to them that are round about us”: everybody hates us. Remember the Arab man who said the whole world is anti-black, every religion is anti-black: not just the Arabs, everybody.

“Thou makest us a byword among the heathen”: they have nicknames for us, whatever. “A shaking of the head among the people”: when we come around, they shake their heads. Look at this: you want to move into the neighborhood here?

“My confusion is continually before me, and the shame of my face hath covered me”. Why our confusion? There are two reasons. First, this was Korah, who saw it in the vision: we were the top nation, and Korah is seeing us go down to the bottom, the worst. He is confused at what he sees, because you can’t be sitting in the seats of authority and see a future of us as slaves.

Now bring it up to today: our people are confused. We go to school, we get our education, we talk like them, we walk like them, and we want to be accepted. Like in The Vernon Johns Story: what do they call a black man with a doctorate? Nigga. A lot of our people in politics and Christianity are confused: why are we being incarcerated at a high rate, murdered in the streets, harassed by cops, losing jobs? Some 300,000 black women just got fired in Trump’s purge of DEI, the most educated, who wore the fake hair, lightened their complexion, talked like them, and still got put out. Jasmine Crockett had more education than all those congressmen, and they moved her district line.

But that’s part of God’s plan. We were not brought to this country to prosper and stay here. We were brought to this country to serve out our punishment and repent, and then go back to greatness. Christians don’t understand that.

“For the voice of him that reproacheth and blasphemeth; by reason of the enemy and avenger.” At one time we knew the white man was our enemy. Now we see him as our avenger: Mr. White man, can you help me with this, that and the other? A few decades ago he was your enemy; now he’s your lover, your bosom buddy, your avenger. Are you kidding me? It makes no sense.
“Yea, for thy sake are we killed all the day long; we are counted as sheep for the slaughter.” This is where Paul got Romans 8:36.

precepts.why: “As it is written, For thy sake we are killed all the day long; we are accounted as sheep for the slaughter.” That’s prophecy right there. Where do you think Paul got it? From Psalms 44:22. That’s why he always said, bring the books and the parchments: the letters he was going to write would reference things already written in the Old Testament.

“Then shall they deliver you up to be afflicted, and shall kill you: and ye shall be hated of all nations for my name’s sake.” When the Arab man said everybody is anti-black, this verse comes right back to mind. He didn’t lie: Christ said everybody’s against us. Everybody.

“As for us, our eyes as yet failed for our vain help”: the vain help is our enemies and our avengers. We want them to avenge us, and that is vain help. “In our watching we have watched for a nation that could not save us”: oh, help us, America.

The most insulting case: the woman who murdered Botham Jean. A black woman in the court stroked the murderer’s blonde hair, the judge came off the bench, hugged her and gave her a Bible, and a brother forgave her, because Jesus said forgive. Only black people. It’s insane.

sense.text:
America’s 250th celebrates the Declaration of Independence, where they said, we hold these truths to be self-evident, that all men are created equal, and for some reason negroes think that included them. Some of y’all went to school and said that’s us. When a wrestler called Michelle Obama a man at the 250th celebration, Charlamagne said it was a reminder that people like that don’t look at black people as equal. His mind is gone; he really believes in the Declaration of Independence. There is no Bible scripture that says all men are created equal. You can search till you’re blue in the face; you won’t find it.

But here is what is in the Bible. Get mad if you want: “For thou art an holy people unto the Lord thy God: the Lord thy God hath chosen thee to be a special people unto himself, above all people that are upon the face of the earth.” That’s not equality. God said, I chose you, I love you, I’m setting you above everybody. Here comes the black man: oh no, we’re equal. Christians do the same thing: we’ve got to be equal. When a white man talks about equality, it means them at the top and you at the bottom, with the Chinese and the Arabs somewhere in the middle. That’s their form of equality.

In 1965, the year black people got their civil rights, a southern judge said it plainly on camera: this is the history of the South, we’ve been brought up like this, we teach our children like this and they’ll teach their children like that; the negro is not a part of my family; the southern way of life, with the negro and his place at the heart of it. He taught his kids that hatred in the 60s. Those kids are 60 or 70 now, and they taught their kids and grandkids the same thing. Some of y’all think they changed. They didn’t change. They are your judges, your politicians, some of them your doctors; it is better for black people to have black doctors, and the highest rate of black babies dying is in Mississippi.

“Because thou hast had a perpetual hatred, and hast shed the blood of the children of Israel by the force of the sword in the time of their calamity, in the time that their iniquity had an end”. When our iniquity had an end, as we read in Zechariah 1:15, they helped forward our affliction; they didn’t show us any mercy. They saw us building cities and towns and said, let’s destroy them. They created a system to check on our kids, and through that system separated children from their parents and sent them into orphanages: the welfare system.

And it is still going on: young black people found hanging from a tree on church property and ruled a suicide, beaten to death, mutilated, dismembered and burned, fifteen black bodies since 2025 and still counting, and no news media covering it. This country never cared about us.

precepts.why:
“Thus saith the Lord; For three transgressions of Edom, and for four, I will not turn away the punishment thereof”: it might look like Edom ain’t being punished, but God says, oh no, I’m not going to forget my punishment on them. They will be punished. “Because he did pursue his brother with the sword”: he pursued the Israelites with the sword, “and did cast off all pity”: they had no pity. “And his anger did tear perpetually”: perpetually means forever, the same perpetual hatred Ezekiel speaks of, “and he kept his wrath for ever”.

“But I will send a fire upon Teman, which shall devour the palaces of Bozrah.” Isaiah 34 goes into Christ’s return, when he destroys the capital cities of Edom.

sense.text: “Come down, and sit in the dust, O virgin daughter of Babylon”: the virgin daughter of Babylon is the United States of America, and their race is Esau, Edom. Some will cut on and say, what do you mean Edom, Babylon was the Cushites. Not this one. “Sit on the ground: there is no throne”: your kingdom is finished. “For thou shalt no more be called tender and delicate”: you shall no longer be called Christian, a God-fearing nation.

“For thou hast trusted in thy wickedness: thou hast said, None seeth me”: I can blow up Tulsa, I can destroy Seneca Village, nobody’s going to know we did this. “Thy wisdom and thy knowledge, it hath perverted thee”: all their technology has perverted them. “And thou hast said in thine heart, I am, and none else beside me”: they’re saying that they’re God.

“Therefore shall evil come upon thee”: this is God’s prophecy. “Thou shalt not be able to put it off”: you ain’t going to be able to stop it. “And desolation shall come upon thee suddenly, which thou shalt not know.”

“Stand now with thine enchantments, and with the multitude of thy sorceries”: God is telling you straight that this Babylon deals in witchcraft. “Wherein thou hast laboured from thy youth”: Washington DC was designed by the Freemasons, and a black man, Benjamin Banneker, helped them; its streets form an upside down pentagram with the White House at the bottom point. 1776 is their youth; America is one of the youngest nations on the planet. That five-pointed star is the star some of you black Hebrew Israelites like to wear while barbecuing on their 4th of July; you should be ashamed of yourselves.

Their sorcery is imagery, the things they put out on television and in movies to manipulate the people, like the Huxtables. A film about the young George Washington dropped in the theaters right at the 250th anniversary; that is no coincidence. They want to bring that patriot spirit back. It’s witchcraft.
“Thou art wearied in the multitude of thy counsels. Let now the astrologers, the stargazers, the monthly prognosticators, stand up, and save thee from these things that shall come upon thee.”

“Behold, they shall be as stubble”: burnt up. “The fire shall burn them; they shall not deliver themselves from the power of the flame: there shall not be a coal to warm at, nor fire to sit before it”: no comfort.

“They shall wander every one to his quarter; none shall save thee”: everyone is going to go back to their homeland.

Every empire that has fallen goes through the same stages: first the death of God, then female sexual liberation. That’s why Trump is trying to bring religion back. They took God out of everything, and now they say, talk about God, because the country is going to be destroyed soon. With this sexual liberation women have two, three, ten partners, and church leaders are calling for a third testament because they despise all the scriptures about the man being over the woman. And Facebook, Google, the internet, digital currency, HD television: all of it is US military technology handed out to watch the people. They can see anything, at any time, from anywhere; that’s why there is an eyeball on the back of the dollar.

precepts.why: Somebody might ask, what do you mean, Edom? Watch what David calls Edom: “Remember, O Lord, the children of Edom in the day of Jerusalem; who said, Rase it, rase it”, destroy it, destroy it, “even to the foundation thereof. O daughter of Babylon, who art to be destroyed”. Edom is the daughter of Babylon. So the virgin daughter of Babylon in Isaiah 47 is Edom: the United States of America.

Some of you think you’re clever: there are two different Babylons, Babylon the great is something else. Shut up and read it. “And a mighty angel took up a stone like a great millstone, and cast it into the sea, saying, Thus with violence shall that great city Babylon be thrown down, and shall be found no more at all.”

“And the light of a candle shall shine no more at all in thee; and the voice of the bridegroom and of the bride shall be heard no more at all in thee: for thy merchants were the great men of the earth”: their corporations. “For by thy sorceries were all nations deceived”: the same sorceries Isaiah speaks of. That is the imagery that goes into sorcery, how they put things out on television and in movies to manipulate the people.

sense.text: We’re back to Job. “Oh that my words were now written! oh that they were printed in a book!” And they are now.
“For I know that my redeemer liveth”: the redeemer is Christ. “And that he shall stand at the latter day upon the earth”: Christ shall stand on the earth in the latter days.

“And though after my skin worms destroy this body”: after I die in this body. “Yet in my flesh shall I see God”: that is regeneration. Job is saying, I’m coming back in the latter days; notice he says, in my flesh.

“Whom I shall see for myself, and mine eyes shall behold, and not another”: his spirit isn’t going to be in another person’s body. It’s going to be his own body, his own eyes looking at the Redeemer. “But ye should say, Why persecute we him, seeing the root of the matter is found in me?” Job understood regeneration. He knew that Christ would return in the latter days and that he would be back to see him for himself. Who Job is today, the Lord knows.

These are the words of Zophar to Job. “That the triumphing of the wicked is short”: we have to believe that, understand that. “And the joy of the hypocrite but for a moment”: the hypocrites are those Christians and Jews who claim they believe in God.

“Though his excellency mount up to the heavens, and his head reach unto the clouds”: that is space travel, that is planes. This goes back to Obadiah 4, setting their nest among the stars. What Job is saying is prophetic.
“Yet he shall perish for ever like his own dung: they which have seen him shall say, Where is he?” When God destroys this man, this hypocrite, we are going to say, where is he?

“He shall fly away as a dream”: imagine this, this man is going to be like a dream when he is taken off the earth. “And shall not be found”. “Yea, he shall be chased away as a vision of the night”: another name for a vision of the night is a nightmare, living under this white man. God says when you wake up it is going to be like a nightmare is over, and you are going to look for that man, and he’s going to be gone.
“The eye also which saw him shall see him no more; neither shall his place any more behold him”: he is going to be off the earth.

“His children shall seek to please the poor, and his hands shall restore their goods.” So don’t worry about reparations. Everything this white man took from us, the Bible says his hands shall restore. Everything he stole is coming back to us. You know how rich the Vatican is: gold, silver, all our records. We are going to get everything back.
“His bones are full of the sin of his youth, which shall lie down with him in the dust.” Like Cain, he has not paid for his crimes yet.

“Though wickedness be sweet in his mouth, though he hide it under his tongue”. When we got those little civil rights, there were certain things the white man could not say anymore. He had to watch calling us the n-word, watch all the name calling; he had to give us jobs. So he hid the wickedness under his tongue. But now he isn’t hiding it anymore: all you immigrants get the f out of our country, all the Haitians out of our country now, calling us the n-word, DEI. It’s all ending now. Remember Kramer from Seinfeld going on that frenzy, cursing black people out: forty years ago you were enslaved and hanging from a tree. These white folks really hate us, and our people still say, I love that show, I love the characters.

“Though he spare it, and forsake it not; but keep it still within his mouth”: it’s still there. Job is saying the same thing Sirach says.
“Yet his meat in his bowels is turned, it is the gall of asps within him”: it’s poison within him.

“He hath swallowed down riches”: that’s what he did, including the Pope. “And he shall vomit them up again”: that’s reparations, that’s restitution. “God shall cast them out of his belly”: wherever he has it hidden, God is going to bring up all the wealth they stole.
“He shall not see the rivers, the floods, the brooks of honey and butter”: he is not going to enjoy the kingdom of heaven. That’s the kingdom.

“That which he laboured for shall he restore, and shall not swallow it down: according to his substance shall the restitution be”: reparations, restitution. So why are you on the street crying for reparations? God says, don’t worry about it, I got you. Everything they took from us is coming back. “And he shall not rejoice therein”: this white man isn’t going to be happy about it, but we don’t give a damn, and God don’t give a damn.

“Because he hath oppressed and hath forsaken the poor”: that’s why we don’t care, because he oppressed us and forsook us. “Because he hath violently taken away an house which he builded not”: he stole homes, houses, lands and people violently. That’s what it’s saying.

“Surely he shall not feel quietness in his belly”: there won’t be any quietness in his belly. “There shall none of his meat be left; therefore shall no man look for his goods”: because it’s all coming to us.

“In the fulness of his sufficiency he shall be in straits: every hand of the wicked shall come upon him.” This is the other nations that are going to attack America for the atrocities, for all the bombings, for all the displacement. Some black Hebrew Israelites say we are going to commit this wickedness, but it says every hand of the wicked: this is proof that it won’t be us walking in righteousness doing this. They attack us like we’re the problem, and they don’t realize the Most High is going to raise up the other nations to come against them, and they’re going to entreat them very, very badly.

“When he is about to fill his belly, God shall cast the fury of his wrath upon him, and shall rain it upon him while he is eating”: that goes with 1 Thessalonians 5, when they shall say peace and safety, then sudden destruction.
“He shall flee from the iron weapon”: the iron weapon is the missiles, the ICBMs. “And the bow of steel shall strike him through.”
